title: Check yourself: what a method can change

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A loyalty service holds `Long balance = 1200L` and calls `addPoints(balance, 250)`. The method `addPoints(Long balance, long earned)` runs `balance += earned;` and then logs `"balance now " + balance`. What does the log show, and what does the caller's `balance` hold afterwards?

options.text: The log shows 1450 and the caller's balance holds 1450, since += updates the Long object that both variables refer to
options.says: a Long can't be changed; += unboxes, adds and boxes a new Long into the parameter only

options.text: The log shows 1450 and the caller's balance holds 1200, since += puts a new Long into the method's own variable
options.says: the parameter is a copy of the caller's reference; += assigns a new Long to that copy, which the log reads and the caller never sees

options.text: The log shows 1200 and the caller's balance holds 1200, since a Long can't be changed and so += leaves the variable as it was
options.says: += on a Long variable assigns a new Long to that variable, so the method's own variable does hold 1450

options.text: The log shows 1200 and the caller's balance holds 1450, since += on a parameter takes effect in the caller's variable on return
options.says: nothing is copied back when a method returns; an assignment to a parameter never reaches the caller's variable

origin.section: An Immutable Argument Can't Be Changed, So a Method That Computes a New Value Returns It

questions.stem: A sensor job holds `int[] readings = {4, 8, 15}` and calls `calibrate(readings)`. The method `calibrate(int[] r)` runs `r[0] = 0; r = Arrays.copyOf(r, 4); r[3] = 16; r[1] = 9;`. What does the caller's `readings` hold afterwards?

options.text: {0, 8, 15}, since the writes after `r = Arrays.copyOf(r, 4)` go to the new array
options.says: r[0] = 0 went to the caller's array; after the assignment r refers to the copy, so r[3] and r[1] change only the copy

options.text: {0, 9, 15}, since the writes through `r` all go to the array the caller passed
options.says: after r is assigned the copy, the writes through r go to the copy, not to the caller's array

options.text: {0, 9, 15, 16}, since the assignment to `r` gives the caller's variable the longer array
options.says: assigning to a parameter never changes the caller's variable; Java has no pass by reference

options.text: {4, 8, 15}, since the array is copied for the method when `readings` is passed
options.says: passing copies the reference, not the array; r[0] = 0 changed the caller's array

origin.section: Java Copies Every Argument, So Assigning to a Parameter Never Reaches the Caller's Variable

questions.stem: After a review, `normalise(final List<String> emails)` has `final` on its parameter. Its body is `emails.replaceAll(String::toLowerCase);` followed by `emails = List.copyOf(emails);`. What does javac do with the method?

options.text: It rejects the replaceAll line, since a final parameter's list can't be changed
options.says: final stops the parameter from being assigned, not the list from changing; replaceAll compiles

options.text: It rejects the assignment line, since a final parameter can't be given another value
options.says: javac reports `final parameter emails may not be assigned` for the assignment and accepts replaceAll

options.text: It accepts both lines, since final on a parameter only constrains the code that calls the method
options.says: final on a parameter constrains the method's body: assigning to it is a compile error

options.text: It rejects both lines, since final makes the parameter and the list it refers to read-only
options.says: final makes only the parameter unassignable; the list can still be changed through it

origin.section: Java Copies Every Argument, So Assigning to a Parameter Never Reaches the Caller's Variable

questions.stem: `record Route(String id, List<String> stops)` declares no constructor of its own. A planner holds an `ArrayList` named `stops` with Depot, Mill Road and Station, creates `new Route("R7", stops)`, and then calls `stops.remove("Depot")` to plan the next route. What does the route's `stops()` return?

options.text: Mill Road and Station, since the route's component refers to the same list the planner changed
options.says: a record's constructor stores its components as given, so the route and the planner share one list

options.text: Mill Road and Station, since a record wraps a list component in a read-only view of the argument
options.says: a record's constructor stores the reference as given; it wraps nothing

options.text: Depot, Mill Road and Station, since a record copies each list component it is given
options.says: a record copies nothing unless its compact constructor does, for example with List.copyOf

options.text: Depot, Mill Road and Station, since a record's components are final and so their lists can't change
options.says: final stops the field from being reassigned, not the list it refers to from changing

origin.section: A Method That Keeps Its Argument Keeps the Caller's Object

questions.stem: `List<String> pickList(List<String> skus)` drops discontinued SKUs with `skus.removeIf(discontinued::contains)` and returns `skus`. The warehouse calls it with its own `ArrayList`. The store app calls it with `List.of("A1", "B2")`, and neither SKU is discontinued. What happens?

options.text: The store app gets UnsupportedOperationException, since its list refuses removeIf even with nothing to remove
options.says: every method of a List.of list that could change it throws, even when the call would change nothing

options.text: The store app gets A1 and B2 back, since its list refuses removeIf only when something would be removed
options.says: a List.of list throws from removeIf even when nothing matches

options.text: The warehouse's list keeps its discontinued SKUs, since the method removes them from its copy of the list
options.says: the method gets a copy of the reference, not of the list; removeIf changes the warehouse's own list

options.text: The warehouse's list keeps its discontinued SKUs, since removeIf builds a new list that the method returns
options.says: removeIf is one of the methods that change the list they are called on; the method changes the warehouse's own list

origin.section: A Method That Changes Its Argument Makes That Change Part of Its Contract

concepts: final on a parameter makes assigning to it a compile error but still lets the method change the object it refers to.
String, the wrappers and BigDecimal can't be changed, so subtract, ++ and += only give the parameter a new object, and a method that computes a new value must return it.
A record's canonical constructor stores its components as given, and a final field doesn't stop the list it refers to from changing.
Every method of an unmodifiable list that could change it throws UnsupportedOperationException, even when the call would change nothing.
